correctness.rationale: Direct occupancy-indicator calculation yields E[M], E[G], and the off-diagonal joint moment (same species cannot be unseen and singleton). The uniform specialization is strictly negative because (1-2/a)<(1-1/a)^2. The one-core plus m rare species coupling gives the stated positive fixed-n limit; rare collisions have probability at most binom(n,2)(1-q)^2/m and missing rare mass is at most n(1-q)/m. The covariance perturbation inequality yields the conservative explicit finite-m bound. Independent Poisson category counts give Cov(M_t,G_t)=-sum_i p_i^2 exp(-2tp_i). An independently coded exact rational calculation gives 5801/12800000 at n=3,q=1/2,m=10 and checks the earlier result normalization for n=2..13.
residual_risks: Assumes finite iid categorical sampling; the rare-tail limit fixes n and core mass; finite bound is not optimal; no claim about estimator correlation.
